stem: A client who takes a high-dose diuretic is starting lisinopril. Which complication should the nurse monitor for most closely during initiation?

options.A: Symptomatic hypotension, particularly if the client is volume or salt depleted.
options.B: Severe hypertension caused by an immediate vasoconstrictor effect of lisinopril.
options.C: Hypervolemia caused by predictable sodium retention from combining an ACE inhibitor with a diuretic.
options.D: Acute hypoglycemia caused by a direct insulin-like effect of lisinopril.

rationale: The current DailyMed lisinopril label states that lisinopril can cause symptomatic hypotension and lists high-dose diuretic therapy and severe volume or salt depletion among risk factors for excessive hypotension. Initiation in such patients requires close supervision and follow-up. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize that high-dose diuretic therapy and volume/salt depletion increase the risk of symptomatic hypotension when lisinopril is initiated.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
source_version_date: Drug label information updated December 17, 2025; prescribing information revised June 2023
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.4 Hypotension: lisinopril can cause symptomatic hypotension; high-dose diuretic therapy and severe volume/salt depletion increase risk. Drug Interactions §7.1 Diuretics: initiation in patients on diuretics may cause excessive blood-pressure reduction.
source_claim_supported: Patients receiving high-dose diuretics or who are volume/salt depleted are at increased risk for symptomatic/excessive hypotension when lisinopril is initiated.

source_original.stem: A client who takes a high-dose diuretic is starting lisinopril. Which complication should the nurse monitor for most closely during initiation?

options.A: Symptomatic hypotension, particularly if the client is volume or salt depleted.
options.B: Severe hypertension caused by an immediate vasoconstrictor effect of lisinopril.
options.C: Hypervolemia caused by predictable sodium retention from combining an ACE inhibitor with a diuretic.
options.D: Acute hypoglycemia caused by a direct insulin-like effect of lisinopril.

source_original.rationale: Lisinopril labeling identifies patients who are volume- or salt-depleted, including those receiving diuretics, as being at increased risk for excessive or symptomatic hypotension.
source_original.source_detail: §5.4 Hypotension. DailyMed label currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: medication administration, controlled substances, adverse effects/interactions, monitoring and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the key A and risk-factor construct, added exact §7.1 diuretic-interaction support, updated current DailyMed metadata, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the item applies a direct label warning.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Lisinopril initiation with high-dose diuretic therapy
audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed lisinopril label; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: DailyMed drug-label information updated 2025-12-17 and live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately links high-dose diuretic/volume depletion to symptomatic hypotension risk during lisinopril initiation.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; lisinopril lowers blood pressure rather than producing an immediate vasoconstrictor hypertensive effect.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; the label does not describe predictable sodium-retention hypervolemia from this combination.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; hypoglycemia is not a direct insulin-like effect and is not the primary initiation risk in this scenario.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A corresponds to the labeled high-dose-diuretic initiation risk.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are parallel adverse-effect interpretations with comparable length.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — adverse effects/interactions and monitoring.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the current lisinopril label §§5.4/7.1, all options, rationale, objective and blueprint mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
